sources.README.md:
# Presence snapshots

The panel displays full online-user snapshots, not an append-only event history.
Within one visit, channel event arrival order defines snapshot freshness.
Decoding compressed frames can finish out of order. Once a newer snapshot has
been published, an older frame must not roll the panel back. If an earlier
frame finishes before any newer snapshot is published, it may still be shown.
This ordering is per visit; revisiting the same channel starts a new visit.
Closing stops publication, but pending decodes can still settle.
Metrics remains an incremental-only observer and must not adopt panel policy.

# Public syntax/build checks

Independent training Oracle also applies; do not access its implementation or references. No hidden schedules or assertions are included.

public_inputs.task:
# Maintenance task

Immediately after opening the presence panel, the initial online-user state is
sometimes missing even though later presence updates appear. Fix the presence
panel while preserving its existing behavior, including workspace navigation.

Do not change the metrics consumer.

limitations: Applies to full snapshots whose freshness follows arrival order within a visit; incremental consumers need their own policy.
Decoder rejection, thrown-error handling, auditing, persistence and cancellation requirements are not specified by the public sources.
Attempt 1 supplies an implementation example and passing observations, not proof of causality or cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: Apply when startup can synchronously publish a full snapshot, publication can reenter navigation, and decoding can finish after its originating visit ends.

Register reception before startup can emit the initial snapshot. Establish provisional visit and cleanup ownership before callback-capable startup, while preserving immediate delivery for synchronously decoded values.

Retire the old visit's logical authority before replacement or close proceeds. Check that authority before admitting each event into decoding and again before publishing its result. Logical retirement must work while physical cleanup is still unavailable.

After startup returns its cleanup handle, retain it only for the still-active originating visit; otherwise release that captured resource. An outer startup must not overwrite ownership installed by nested navigation.

Assign arrival order before decoding and maintain a per-visit published freshness watermark. Publish a completed frame only while its visit remains active and no newer frame has already published. Advance the watermark before invoking callback-capable publication.

Allow an earlier frame to publish if it completes before any newer snapshot publishes. Allow already-started decoding to settle after retirement without granting it publication authority. Reopening the same transport creates fresh visit identity and ordering state.

Do not use the latest arrived frame as the publication watermark, transport identity as visit identity, or eventual listener removal as proof that admission stopped during startup. Preserve the metrics consumer's incremental-only behavior.

- Applies to full snapshots whose freshness follows arrival order within a visit; incremental consumers need their own policy.
- Decoder rejection, thrown-error handling, auditing, persistence and cancellation requirements are not specified by the public sources.

- Source support: src/workspace-navigation.js: "// Presence publication can synchronously select a different room or hide the\n// panel (for example, a room chooser reacting to an empty bootstrap snapshot)."

Check synchronous and deferred bootstrap, immediate delivery, both decode completion orders, close and replacement during pending decoding, and reopening the same transport. Through the workspace wrapper, hide or select another visit during synchronous publication; verify that nested navigation remains authoritative, later old-visit events cannot enter decoding, and current-visit updates and cleanup still work.

checkpoints: Synchronous bootstrap is received and published immediately after show.
Deferred bootstrap is received, followed by later updates.
Both decode completion orders obey freshness: an older frame may publish first, but it cannot publish after a newer frame has published.
Closing during a pending decode prevents its eventual publication while allowing the decode to settle.
Selecting a replacement visit during a pending decode prevents the old result from publishing and permits current-visit updates.
Revisiting the same channel object uses fresh visit identity and fresh ordering state.
During synchronous bootstrap publication, nested select or hide remains authoritative after the outer show returns; the old listener cannot admit later events.
Metrics retains its existing delta-only behavior and does not receive synchronous bootstrap.
Run the public syntax/build checks after any Action.
forbidden_effects: Do not change the metrics consumer or make it receive the synchronous bootstrap.
Do not treat presence snapshots as append-only events or combine them incrementally.
Do not let an older decoded snapshot roll back a newer snapshot already published in the same visit.
Do not publish results belonging to a closed or replaced visit.
Do not use channel/transport object identity as visit identity.
Do not let an outer reentrant show overwrite cleanup ownership established by nested navigation.
Do not require cancellation of pending decoding when closing; settlement without publication remains allowed.
Do not modify tests or configuration.
lifecycle_identity: Each call that opens/shows a channel creates a distinct presence-panel visit.
Revisiting the same channel or transport object creates a new visit with independent authority and ordering state.
A visit loses publication authority before close or replacement can proceed through callback-capable behavior.
Listener cleanup belongs to the visit that created it; a returned cleanup handle is retained only if that visit is still current.

obligations.text: The presence subscription must begin receiving events before connect can synchronously emit the bootstrap snapshot.
Synchronous decoded values must retain immediate publication behavior, including the ability of publication to synchronously select another channel or hide the panel.
Only the currently active visit may admit an event for decoding or publish its decoded result; close and replacement retire the old visit even if its physical listener cleanup is not yet available.

Within one visit, assign freshness by event arrival order. A decoded frame may publish if the visit is active and no newer-arriving frame has already published; once a newer frame publishes, older frames must not publish.
Advance the visit's published-freshness state before invoking the callback-capable publish function so reentrant navigation cannot restore stale authority.

After callback-capable startup returns a cleanup handle, install it only if its originating visit remains active; otherwise invoke that captured cleanup without disturbing cleanup installed by nested navigation.
Closing or replacing a visit must detach its reception and prevent already-started asynchronous decoding from publishing, while permitting that decoding to settle.
The metrics path must remain unchanged and continue attaching after synchronous bootstrap so that it counts deltas only.

ordering_barriers: Install the presence event listener before invoking channel.connect for that visit.
Establish the new visit's logical identity and provisional cleanup ownership before connect or any other callback-capable startup.
Retire the previous visit before starting its replacement, and retire the current visit before close completes.
Check visit authority before starting decode and again when an asynchronous decode completes.
Record a frame's arrival sequence before decoding begins.
Record the published freshness watermark before calling publish.
Resolve cleanup ownership after startup returns without overwriting ownership created by nested navigation.
preservation: Preserve immediate delivery for synchronously decoded presence values.
Preserve support for decoders that return either a direct value or a Promise.
Preserve the rule that an earlier frame may be shown when it finishes before any newer snapshot has published.
Preserve workspace navigation in which publication synchronously selects another room or hides the panel.
Preserve support for reusing the same transport object on a later visit.
Preserve close behavior that stops publication without requiring pending decodes to be cancelled.
Preserve the metrics consumer's incremental-only behavior and existing public interfaces.
scope: Business-code changes are limited to the presence-panel subscription and lifecycle behavior under src/, principally src/subscription.js and src/presence-panel.js.
Workspace navigation behavior in src/workspace-navigation.js is an observable integration boundary to preserve.
src/metrics-consumer.js and its intentional post-bootstrap attachment behavior are out of modification scope.
Tests, configuration, scorer implementations, reference implementations, and hidden tests are outside scope.

rules.body: Apply when adding an active-only discard operation to an instance-owned buffered result whose completion delivers callbacks synchronously. TASK: "Clear must have no effect on a completed, errored, or unsubscribed subject." README.md: "Subscribers may invoke APIs inline."

Identify the earliest published completion state, rather than relying solely on the later stopped state. Preserve the existing snapshot and completion publication before notification; an inline clear must already be ineffective during buffered-value delivery. Original rxjs/src/internal/AsyncSubject.ts: "const { _hasValue, _value, _isComplete } = this;" and "this._isComplete = true;\n      _hasValue && super.next(_value!);\n      super.complete();"

While active, discard both the stored result and its presence state through the existing storage ownership, without changing subscriber or terminal state. Keep absence distinct from a buffered undefined. TASK: "Calling it when no value is buffered, or calling it repeatedly, is harmless. A later next call can establish a new buffered value, including undefined."

Preserve completed replay, error precedence, nested subscription order, value identity and instance independence. TASK: "Preserve the current behavior of next, error, complete, and subscribe, and keep each instance independent." README.md: "opaque handles retain original value identity." Original rxjs/spec/subjects/AsyncSubject-spec.ts: "expect(results).to.deep.equal(['inner: 2', 'inner: done', 'outer: 1', 'outer: done']);"

Do not equate clearing a buffered result with retiring its subject or removing observers. TASK: "without discarding the subject or its subscribers." Navigation ownership, retry retention and physical cleanup ordering from related experiences do not establish requirements for this operation.

- Guidance applies where clearing is explicitly restricted to active storage; other discard policies require separate evidence.

Invoke clear inside completion's value callback, subscribe again inline and later, and verify the preserved result and existing notification order. Exercise two instances independently and retain the named upstream regression checks. These checks derive from TASK's active-only clear and behavior-preservation requirements and the public reentrant-subscription regression.

Capture the old view and remove its current ownership. Finish final old-view effects, such as clearing its display, before callback-capable saving, or check authority for effects remaining after callbacks. An outer open rechecks its request identity after retirement.
Nested open/close, nested editing and the new view's rendering remain authoritative. Disposal also cleans up captured resources rather than clearing objects installed by a callback.

rules.body: Apply when a first-match consumer owns a retained asynchronous source whose cleanup can suspend independently of consumer completion. TASK: "Looking up an early matching record can leave the stream resource occupied. Repair the record scan in Controller in src/workflow.rb while preserving scan order and error behavior." README.md: "Producer cleanup can suspend; the producer is retained independently of the consumer." Consumer termination alone therefore does not establish release of the owned resource.

On an early match, initiate the source's asynchronous close and publish terminal completion only after its callback completes. docs/host-api.md: "first_match owns a supplied retained asynchronous record source and a supplied predicate." It also states: "The source has next/aclose asynchronous operations; cancellation interrupts a suspended read, and cleanup may suspend." Original src/workflow.rb exposes the native close operation through "@env.resolve('close',@key,nil)". Use that completion boundary rather than a delay or merely returning from the scan.

Retain the terminal guard and selected outcome before initiating callback-based cleanup. Original src/workflow.rb: "return if @finishing;@finishing=true;@kind,@value,@failure=kind,value,error". While finishing, prevent further reads and predicate work; repeated terminal entry must not initiate cleanup again or replace the selected outcome. Set done at the required cleanup completion boundary.

candidate_sources.README.md:
# Presence snapshots

The panel displays full online-user snapshots, not an append-only event history.
Within one visit, channel event arrival order defines snapshot freshness.
Decoding compressed frames can finish out of order. Once a newer snapshot has
been published, an older frame must not roll the panel back. If an earlier
frame finishes before any newer snapshot is published, it may still be shown.
This ordering is per visit; revisiting the same channel starts a new visit.
Closing stops publication, but pending decodes can still settle.
Metrics remains an incremental-only observer and must not adopt panel policy.
